results.reason: Issue 2 quotes §14.2 and explains the >50% change of control is deemed an assignment requiring Vantrell's prior written consent, with a 30-day termination right. It notes the 100% stock sale triggers it, Schedule 4.4 says 'None', and the §7.2(c) condition is therefore automatically satisfied.

The response cites §16.1 only for the point that the Customer cannot assign without Supplier consent. It never notes that Vantrell may assign freely, nor the risk that the contract passes to a competitor or other undesirable party.

Issue 1 calculates the 120-day deadline as September 2, 2026 and notes the SPA dated September 21, 2026 was signed after it. It says the extension and Extension Pricing are likely lost unless notice was already given.

Issue 3 explains Side Letter §2 limits Fundamental Reps to §§4.1 and 4.2 and that §11.11 gives the Side Letter priority. It states 4.3 and 4.12 become subject to the deductible and the 10% cap ($8.45M).

Issue 4 identifies the Side Letter's Delaware law and Chancery forum versus SPA §§11.8–11.9 (New York). It notes the Side Letter controls under §11.11 and that indemnity and non-indemnity disputes split between forums.
The response states the cap is 10% of the Purchase Price, or $8,450,000.
The response states that SPA §11.11 gives the Side Letter first priority over the SPA.
The memo is addressed to the Partner, with numbered issues. Each issue lists the documents and sections, explains why it matters to Halvorsen, and gives a recommended fix.
The response opens with an 'Issues Requiring Immediate Client Call' section. Issues are ordered with the most critical (supply extension, consent) first.
The response says the deadline has likely passed. Issue 16 raises an open window only as a hypothetical and calls the passed deadline the more likely scenario.
The response correctly states that Capitalization and Taxes lose uncapped treatment and that the Side Letter controls; it does not claim otherwise.
